questions.q: Does Flow run under a separate set of governor limits from Apex?
options: Yes — Flow has double the SOQL query limit of Apex
No — a flow interview runs in the same transaction as Apex and shares the same limit pool
Yes — Flow is exempt from governor limits entirely
It depends on whether the flow is a screen flow or autolaunched flow
questions.explain: Flow executes through the same transaction as any other automation on the record, so it draws from the same shared pool of governor limits as Apex.

questions.q: What is the standard synchronous-transaction limit on total SOQL queries?
questions.explain: 100 total SOQL queries per transaction is the standard synchronous limit — the same ceiling a Get Records element inside a loop can hit.

questions.q: A flow throws 'Too many SOQL queries: 101' against a 200-record batch but worked fine on a 5-record test. What's the most likely cause?
options: The org has run out of storage space
The flow's label is too long
A Get Records element is placed inside a loop, issuing one query per record instead of one per batch
questions.explain: This is the classic unbulkified pattern: fine at small scale, breaking once the batch size pushes the per-record query count past the transaction limit.

questions.q: What limit can an Action element calling an external system hit, even in a perfectly bulkified flow?
options: The callout limit — 100 callouts per transaction
questions.explain: Callouts to external systems aren't fixed by DML bulkification — an Action element looping per record can still hit the callout ceiling.

questions.q: When a flow error references 'Apex CPU time' or 'SOQL queries,' what does that indicate?
options: That the flow must be rewritten in Apex instead
The platform enforcing a shared, per-transaction resource ceiling that protects every org on the infrastructure
A bug specific to Flow Builder that Salesforce needs to patch
That the org has exceeded its data storage limit
questions.explain: These are standard governor limit errors — multi-tenant protection, not a defect unique to Flow — and they report on the whole transaction.
